implementationSummary: Meta-issued routing correction on #715 (slice B-3): wired the already-computed continuous-trigger scoring output to durable persistence. B-1 (#713) dispatches an injectable scoring_stage after the KPI envelope commits, in an isolated failure domain, gated by CDP_DECISIONS_SCORING_ENABLED (default OFF). B-2 (#714) implemented decision_rules_scoring_stage to call the shared run_daily_scoring_for_shop and return a DailyScoringResult, but never persisted it. B-3 (#715, prior data-platform phase) made services/action_cards/persist.py::persist_scoring_result idempotent by workflow_key, status-preserving for in-flight cards, and computed_at-stamping (migration 026_action_cards_computed_at) — but could not wire it in because services/cdp_speed/ was outside that phase's authorized paths. This increment closes the gap: decision_rules_scoring_stage (backend/src/juli_backend/services/cdp_speed/decision_rules_scoring.py:76) now calls persist_scoring_result(session, job.shop_id, result) after computing the result and before returning it unchanged, reusing the existing persistence boundary with no second write path. shared_compute_orchestrator.py was not touched — its scoring_stage seam, isolated commit/rollback wrapper, and the test_default_scoring_stage_is_wiring_only_stub static guard (forbidding services.scoring/run_daily_scoring_for_shop/action_cards tokens in that file) remain exactly as B-1 left them; persist_scoring_result raises on failure rather than being swallowed, so a persistence error still lands in the orchestrator's own try/except/rollback around the scoring stage, never touching the already-committed KPI envelope. Added tests/unit/test_cdp_speed_decision_rules_scoring_persistence.py exercising the wiring through the public decision_rules_scoring_stage entry point (not by calling persist_scoring_result directly): persistence of ranked candidates as Action Card rows, burst idempotency across three repeated stage calls for the same shop (AC1), and computed_at stamped and queryable per persisted card (AC3). Updated services/cdp_speed/MODULE.md to document decision_rules_scoring_stage's new persist dependency and behavior.
assumptions: Persistence is wired unconditionally inside decision_rules_scoring_stage rather than behind a second feature flag — the existing CDP_DECISIONS_SCORING_ENABLED gate on the B-1 orchestrator seam (default OFF) already controls whether this stage runs at all in production, so a second gate around the persist call inside the stage would be redundant and was out of scope per the task's constraints (no emission budget, B-4/#716).

The prior B-3 (data-platform) implementation-issue-715.json artifact is fully overwritten by this file rather than appended to, because the schema models a single artifact object (additionalProperties: false, no array/history field) — this artifact's implementationSummary and testsAdded reflect only this backend increment; the B-3 persist.py/migration work's own historical detail lives in that commit's diff (74f75f62) rather than being restated here.
risks: No new feature flag gates the persist call itself, only the pre-existing CDP_DECISIONS_SCORING_ENABLED orchestrator-level gate — if that flag is ever flipped on for a shop with a large recommended_workflows fan-out and no emission budget yet (B-4/#716 not landed), every ranked recommendation is persisted as an active candidate with no cap/cooldown/novelty filtering, which is expected/in-scope per this issue's constraints but is a known open follow-up.

services/action_cards/MODULE.md still states that wiring a continuous compute trigger's scoring stage onto persist_scoring_result 'is not owned by this module' — that statement remains literally true (the wiring lives in decision_rules_scoring.py, not persist.py) but now describes a completed fact rather than an open gap; flagged for Meta/B-3 owners to consider whether that note should be refreshed, not edited by this backend executor since action_cards/ is outside this increment's authorized paths.
